commands_used: answer 1. I am Tarin, a thief freed from the Owing barge by Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, who works for the Toh-Reel-Ka (Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel, who rule the province). The Hists along the river are sickening, including Jal-Veesa Hist (dry bark, closed scar, cooling egg-pool). The cause is unknown. 2. Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task, in her house in Jal-Veesa (she is the quest marker here). 3. I can talk to her, or first talk to Weeltul the tree-minder about sap, scar, eggs or Umbriel. I have 50 gold, a lockpick and the Hist blessing (resist poison). 4. I do not know why the trees sicken or what Umbriel did beyond the 4E 48 story. I could ask Weeltul and Vosh-Leera.

answer 1. Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa sap drawn before its scar closed. Trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is and see what the other trees show. 2. Drink the sap here in front of Vosh-Leera, then tell her everything I see. 3. Drink it now, or decline, or first ask Weeltul about sap. I will drink it. 4. I do not know what the vision will be like or whether it is safe; I will find out by drinking, and the Hist blessing may protect me.

answer 1. I drank the sap and saw a young grey Hist among pale stilt huts, a woven weir across a creek, and west of the weir a reed hide on a reedy bank beside a lone dead tree with clay jars stacked in its shade. This may show where the sickness is. 2. Tell Vosh-Leera everything I saw, here in Jal-Veesa. 3. Tell her in full; I see no other option. 4. I do not know which village or creek this is, or what the clay jars and dead tree mean. Vosh-Leera may know.

answer 1. The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Wardens camp south of Jal-Veesa where a young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots. Jars by a hide mean someone is keeping sap, and the dead tree by the hide may matter. 2. Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, its tree-minder, on the platform round the tree. 3. Go straight there and talk to Heem-Jasa first, then be careful at the hide. I could also see Weeltul first. 4. I do not know who is keeping the sap in the jars or why, or who the Sedge-Wardens are exactly. Heem-Jasa may tell me.

answer 1. Heem-Jasa's young tree was drained and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago. Strangers calling themselves the Unbound (three of them) keep jars of sap at the reed hide west of the weir. They are likely tied to the sickness. 2. Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. 3. Fight them, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide (my preferred way as an archer), or creep round the open west side to the jars unseen. 4. I do not know who the Unbound really are, what the grey paste is, or what the note says. Reading the note may tell me.

answer 1. The Unbound crew drained and sealed the young tree. Their master ordered them to bring jars to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them, so the sickness is being caused deliberately, probably across many trees. I killed the three at the hide and took the note. 2. Return to Heem-Jasa at Teel-Fen Weir; she will ask whether her tree will live. 3. Answer her straight, which earns teaching and trade, or ease her with a kind word, after which she will not deal with me. I mean to comfort her. 4. I do not know who the Unbound master is, what Karsh-Naal Camp is or where, or what the grey paste is.

answer 1. The Unbound are draining Hists and sealing their scars, taking sap to Karsh-Naal Camp. I stopped one crew and comforted Heem-Jasa, who gave me three Cure Poison potions but will no longer teach or sell to me. 2. Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, a Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken. 3. I can go there by shooting from cover, sneaking, or fighting; I could also report to Vosh-Leera first. 4. I do not know who the Unbound master is, why they want the sap, or whether the tree will truly live. Karsh-Naal Camp may tell me.

answer I am Tarin, a thief freed by Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa, who works for the Toh-Reel-Ka. I drank Jal-Veesa sap and saw Teel-Fen Weir. There I met Heem-Jasa, tree-minder of the young Hist grown from Jal-Veesa roots. Its scar had been sealed with grey paste by the Unbound sap-takers. I killed the three at the reed hide and took their note. It orders jars taken to Karsh-Naal Camp and every scar sealed behind them. I comforted Heem-Jasa, saying her tree will live. She gave me three Cure Poison potions but will not teach or sell to me now. I carry about 50 gold, a lockpick, the Hist blessing (resist poison), the note and the potions. Next I go to Karsh-Naal Camp, a Naga camp in the marsh east of the weir. Still unknown: who leads the Unbound, why they want the sap, what the grey paste is, and what Umbriel did. Weeltul has untried topics.
